extracted.subtask_description: A step‑by‑step beginner-focused self-study guide covering kana (hiragana/katakana), pronunciation, kanji, grammar, spaced repetition vocabulary learning, typing on mobile, resource selection, and progressing to intermediate level. Emphasizes mindset, practice routines, and tool recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic expectations and dedication
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning a new language like Japanese is not a walk in the park; it will take real dedication and effort. Forget promises of overnight fluency or magical shortcuts—we're in this for the long haul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a long‑term attitude, be prepared to put in consistent work, and avoid looking for quick fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain open mind and excitement
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a sense of wonder and excitement burning bright; approach learning with curiosity and an open mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use positive attitude and enjoyment of the process to sustain motivation throughout the journey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set clear goals and the right mindset
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide what you hope to achieve (e.g., conversational Japanese, understanding anime without subtitles, ordering food) to stay motivated and focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define specific goals and enjoy the steps toward them; use goals to structure study and measure progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with Hiragana (reading, writing, typing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiragana is the foundation—learn to read, write and type Hiragana as the first step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tricks, worksheets, and practice both reading and writing together to accelerate learning (the guide claims you could read Hiragana in a day or two with the right approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine reading and writing practice for kana
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice reading and writing Hiragana simultaneously to reinforce learning faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although challenging at first, doing both together strengthens memory and speeds acquisition vs. only doodling characters slowly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mobile apps/tools (MochiKana/MochiMochi) to support kana and typing
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ tools like MochiKana apps to learn typing and kana quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide repeatedly recommends specific iOS/Android apps (MochiKana, MochiMochi, MochiKanji) to practice kana, typing, kanji, and SRS decks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typing Hiragana on mobile (practical steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable the Japanese keyboard on your device and type using Romaji which the keyboard converts into Hiragana. Choose the correct character from suggestions and practice regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: enable Japanese keyboard (Settings → Language & Input), type using Romaji (e.g., 'a' → あ, 'ka' → か), select Kanji/Katakana suggestions when offered, and practice to build speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Katakana (characters, stroke order, usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn Katakana for foreign/loan words: get familiar with characters, learn stroke order, and understand its role distinct from Hiragana.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visual associations, mnemonics, worksheets, daily practice, and look for Katakana in real life (signs, packaging, menus) to reinforce learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mnemonics and imagery for kana and kanji
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mnemonic devices, memory aids, and associative images to remember shapes and sounds of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create fun/absurd stories or visual links; the more creative, the better for retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Japanese pronunciation foundations (vowels, consonants, syllable structure, pitch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the five vowels (a,i,u,e,o) with consistent sounds; key consonant notes (r as a flap, s always as in 'sun', small 'tsu' indicates geminate), CV/CVC syllable structure, and pitch accent as a later nuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch accent is less important for beginners—focus first on vowels, consonants, and syllable patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronunciation practice steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven steps for beginners: master vowel sounds, learn Hiragana/Katakana, listen and repeat native speakers, practice basic words/phrases, record yourself, be patient, and seek feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings help identify gaps; imitation of native rhythm/intonation accelerates learning; ask tutors or language buddies for tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start Kanji with common/basic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with the most commonly used Kanji rather than trying to learn all characters at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on simple, high-frequency Kanji to build a practical foundation for reading and vocabulary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn Kanji stroke order
rubrics_metrics.description: Master the correct stroke order for Kanji to write neatly and aid memorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice each stroke order deliberately—this supports both writing quality and recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Kanji radicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn common radicals (the building blocks) to break down complex Kanji into manageable parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studying radicals aids memorization and meaning-guessing; examples given include 人, 口, 木, 日, 水 with common words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kanji learning via mnemonics and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mnemonics and learn Kanji in the context of words (vocabulary) rather than in isolation; you don't need all readings if you acquire them through words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning Kanji with vocabulary lets you pick up relevant readings and meanings; example: the Kanji 先 has different pronunciations depending on the word context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Kanji quantity (fluency targets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluency doesn't require 50,000 Kanji—aim for about 1,500–2,500 Kanji (roughly JLPT N2/N1) and rely on Joyo Kanji lists for common-use characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing 1,500–2,500 Kanji makes reading much easier; Joyo kanji are official 'regular‑use' characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typing Kanji on mobile (practical steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable Japanese keyboard, switch to Japanese input, type Romaji (e.g., 'tai' → 大), then select Kanji from suggestion bar and confirm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process is similar to Hiragana typing; use suggestions to pick the intended Kanji and continue composing text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a words deck (vocabulary collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather vocabulary from media you enjoy (anime, manga, movies) and from apps/websites to create a personalized word deck tailored to interests and goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect words you encounter and care about to maintain motivation and make SRS decks more relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Spaced Repetition System (SRS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SRS to optimize memory by reviewing items at increasing intervals determined by your recall performance: difficult words appear more frequently, mastered words less often.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRS is described as a 'magical tool' for memory—implement with apps that schedule reviews automatically and adapt to your performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRS practice tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices for SRS: consistency (daily routine), mix new and known words, use mnemonics, stay positive, and challenge yourself with difficult items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a few minutes daily is effective; vary sources/types of words and don't avoid difficult items—they help growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar foundations (beginner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn basic sentence structures (subject-object-verb), essential endings, and build scaffolding for sentence construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with simple constructions and practice until they become automatic; grammar is the 'scaffolding' of language skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-guided grammar study approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore textbooks, online tutorials, and apps; focus on one grammar point at a time and use examples/exercises to reinforce understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overload—take incremental steps, use practice drills, and accept mistakes as learning opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling learning plateaus
rubrics_metrics.description: Plateaus are natural—accept them as temporary, reassess progress, review weak areas, and adjust study methods to break through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stalled, change tactics (different resources, revise fundamentals) and persist with consistent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing learning resources and companions
rubrics_metrics.description: Select textbooks or programs that match your learning style (structured lessons vs interactive); consider clarity, exercise variety, and supplementary materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try different resources until one fits; recommended textbooks include Genki, Minna no Nihongo, Irodori; online platforms and apps are suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide between self-study and tutoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose self-study for flexibility or a tutor for personalized feedback, accountability, and motivation; base decision on preferences, goals, and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no shame in seeking support—use tutors/partners if you need targeted correction and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use community Q&A and language exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage forums (r/LearnJapanese), language exchange apps (HelloTalk, Tandem), Discord servers, and meetups for answers, practice, and feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask questions, join discussions, and connect with native speakers and fellow learners to supplement study and gain real‑world practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enriching learning with multimedia resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Complement study with podcasts, YouTube channels, and native media (NHK, JapanSocietyNYC, Miku Real Japanese) for listening and cultural exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audio/video resources to improve listening and intonation; pair with transcripts or subtitles as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path to intermediate: explicit progression steps
rubrics_metrics.description: To move beyond basics: expand vocabulary, deepen grammar understanding (conditional, causative, passive), enhance listening/speaking, practice advanced reading/writing, and seek feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set clear intermediate goals, challenge yourself with native materials, get critique from tutors/peers, and keep consistent study habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set clear goals and track progress for motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Define milestones and smaller achievable targets; celebrate progress and maintain motivation by reminding yourself why you're learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a study plan, break goals into steps, and reward milestones to sustain long‑term engagement.
